result.name: Authority composition is a meet calculation with an explicit proof dependency graph
result.statement: For every node v, a(v) is the meet of c(w) over all ancestors w of v, including v. It is the largest profile simultaneously bounded by all those caps. Adding an additional dependency can only decrease or preserve the profile.
result.proof: Order the graph topologically. The claim is immediate for a source. Enlarging the ancestor set introduces further meet factors and cannot raise any coordinate. None of these steps supplies a proof that an individual premise is true: that requires a separately checked derivation. definitions: A finite commutative ring R has an explicitly enumerable underlying set and computable addition and multiplication tables. An ideal is a subset containing zero, closed under addition and multiplication by all ring elements.
A maximal proper ideal is a proper ideal contained in no strictly larger proper ideal. A finite search is constructive when it returns a witness with a terminating verification.

result.name: A finite maximal-ideal algorithm separates constructive witnesses from unrestricted choice
result.statement: Every finite nonzero commutative unital ring has a maximal proper ideal, and exhaustive search returns one. For Z/12Z the maximal ideals are (2) and (3), giving quotient fields F₂ and F₃.
